implementation_notes: JavaScript's clones are the most common of any language in the catalogue and the hardest to remove safely, because the dynamic typing that makes copying easy also makes the shared abstraction awkward to type. The characteristic cases are fetch handlers that differ only in a URL and a transform, form validation rules pasted into several components, and utility functions copied from a blog post. The cross-language case deserves particular attention: the MSR study of over 20,000 Eclipse users found more than 75,000 copy-paste incidents across different programming languages, so the same logic in a frontend and a backend is a normal occurrence and no single-language detector will find it. ESLint's `sonarjs/no-duplicate-string` and jscpd are the instruments.
idiom_name: copy-pasted fetch handlers; duplicated form validation
pitfalls: Utility functions copied from a blog post are duplicated in every project that used the same post, and the copy usually carries the original's bugs.
Validation rules pasted into each component are the most common frontend clone and the one most likely to be updated in only one place.
Copy-paste across the frontend/backend boundary is normal and invisible to both linters; it needs a shared schema, not a shared module.
